html:
In March 1521 the Spanish expedition of Ferdinand Magellan reached the islands now called the Philippines, after the first crossing of the Pacific by Europeans. It was the first European contact with the islands.

Magellan, a Portuguese captain sailing for Spain, had set out in 1519 to reach the Spice Islands by sailing west. The crossing of the Pacific took over three months and many of his men died of hunger and scurvy. In the islands he held a Christian mass, and at Cebu he won over the ruler Rajah Humabon, who was baptised with hundreds of his people.

Magellan then tried to force the chief of nearby Mactan, Lapulapu, to submit. On 27 April 1521 Magellan was killed in the Battle of Mactan; Filipinos remember Lapulapu as the first to resist European rule. The survivors sailed on to the Moluccas, and one ship under Juan Sebastián Elcano returned to Spain in 1522, completing the first voyage around the world. Spain came back in 1565 to colonise the islands; see Manila galleons.
